title: Example 17-4: Partial Word Blanks

illustrates.quote: Lines Indicating Omitted Parts of Words. When text refers to spelling or word structure: a. Follow print for whatever symbol is used to represent a blank to be filled in. b. If applicable, use contractions in the portions of the word attached to the low line or other symbol.

blocks.text: The tunnels in Boston are very perplex_.

print.notes: Five unconnected sentences, each with a solid low-line blank standing in for the omitted word part (print shows a run of underscores; braille shows ONE dot-46,36 blank symbol per gap, not one cell per underscore — distinct from Example 17-5's per-letter asterisk convention).
print.printFeatures: Five short sentences with an underscore blank; the surrounding letters keep their normal contractions (17.9.1b).

braille.notes: Byte-identical between A and B; matches independent re-extraction exactly.

resolution: Both runs (A, B) came from the same model (Gemini Pro via Antigravity, 17 Sep 2026) and are not independent; agreement was treated as no evidence. braille.lines independently re-extracted from references/_text/braille-formats-2016.txt (the line-number field, digits + >=3 spaces, or the fixed left margin measured in ASCII spaces before any U+2800 cell, stripped by counting; U+2800->space; trailing spaces removed). Braille and rule id unchanged (both agreed '17.9.1', matches source). Modeled as five ordinary paragraphs, each with a single literal underscore standing for the blank-fill symbol; the surrounding words keep normal contraction so 17.9.1b's requirement is exercised automatically (no special code needed). Whether a literal '_' translates through louis to the same dot-46,36 symbol the book calls '.-' is the mismatch this file actually tests — if not, that is a genuine, new gap (no existing finding names it), not a modeling error.
